result:
No actions this turn.

Understood. I'll write it up. One choice is still open first: how it gets built. It changes the design, so I'd rather you pick it than find my guess in the document.

**1. Add it to the taproom app (my recommendation).** Batch tracking becomes a new section of the Flask app already on the office Pi. It gets its own tables in the same SQLite database. You keep one program to run, one login and one file to back up. The cost is a shared fate. A bad update to the tabs side could take batch tracking down too, and the reverse is also true.

**2. A separate small app on the same Pi.** Same tools, but its own program and its own database file. A taproom problem can't touch your trace records. The cost is two things to start, update and back up.

I dropped hosted brewery software such as Ekos or Breww. They do traceability well, but they cost a monthly fee, need the internet on brew day, and don't build on what you have.

The scanner works the same way in both options. A standard USB barcode scanner acts like a keyboard, so it types the lot number into a form on whatever screen the brewers use.

This is a project-sized piece of work. So I'll write a full design document into the repo. A reviewer will read it before you do, and I may come back once with a few questions from that read.

Which way do you want to go, or should I just use option 1?
